question: The former Industria Ambientale Organizzata (I.A.O.) site in Giardinetto Agro, in the municipality of Troia (Foggia), is one of the biggest environmental emergencies in Puglia. According to publicly available data, the site covers around 40 hectares, allegedly contains over 300 000 tonnes of waste, and benefits from public funding of around EUR 49 million, including EUR 19.

85 million from Italy’s national recovery and resilience plan (NRRP)1. According to recent press reports and tip-offs from the public2, the emergency safety works would seem to have been substantially slowed down or halted since the end of 2025.

Despite the considerable use of public money, up-to-date information on the state of progress of the works, how much they are costing and whether they are running to schedule is not easily accessible. In view of the above: 1.
Does the Commission have any information on the progress of the emergency safety works and the reasons for the possible slowdowns or suspensions of activity reported since the end of 2025?
What checks have been carried out on the use of EU and NRRP resources allocated to the project and the reporting thereof?
Does the Commission intend to ask the competent Italian authorities for an updated public report on the state of play, the resources used and the expected timeframe for completing the project?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (11.8.2026) The Commission monitors the implementation of the Italian national recovery and resilience plan (RRP) based on the legal requirements outlined in the Annex to the Council Implementing Decision on the approval of the assessment of Italy’s RRP1.

Regarding the investment on the remediation of ‘orphan-sites soil’, target M2C4-25 of Italy’s RRP will be assessed in the context of the tenth payment request, expected to be submitted by Italy in September 2026. The target concerns the issuance of certificates of soil remediation2 for 70% of the surface of orphan sites listed in the Action Plan3.

It follows milestone M2C424, which consisted of adopting an Action Plan4 for the identification and revitalisation of orphan sites, assessed under the third payment request. The former Industria Ambientale Organizzata site in Giardinetto Agro, in the municipality of Troia (Foggia), is divided into lots. According to the latest Action Plan5, only interventions for lot 2.

a are financed by the Italian RRP, for a total of EUR 19.85 million. This lot has a surface of 74 000 square metres. In line with the applicable legal framework of the Recovery and Resilience Facility, Member States must meet all milestones and targets by 31 August 2026, and the Commission must make the final payments by 31 December 2026.

Should the Commission assess that any milestone or target is not satisfactorily met, it can take action in line with Article 24 of Regulation (EU) 2021/2416. Member States remain primarily responsible for the implementation of their RRPs as approved in the Annex to the Council Implementing Decision, and for verifying that the financing provided has been properly used in accordance with all applicable rules.
